mission: Aftermath of the debate — Kael and Desh's first real interaction. Kael watches Desh work on the ship and makes a dry observation. The non-Force friendship begins.
why_now: The Force-users have been arguing about the Force. Desh — the only person who can't feel any of it — and Kael — the person most cynical about all of it — find unexpected common ground.
conflict: Kael's detachment vs. Desh's practical engagement. Kael expects Desh to be a tool of Ben's, like he was a tool of the Sith. Instead, Desh is here by choice — a concept Kael is still processing.
turning_point: Desh asks Kael to hand him a hydrospanner without any philosophical freight — just one person asking another for help. Kael stares for a beat, then hands it over. Smallest gesture. Biggest meaning.
opening_hook: The silence after the debate is louder than the debate. Desh breaks it by banging on a conduit that's been cycling wrong since the extra passengers came aboard.
closing_hook: Kael, watching Desh work: 'You don't feel any of it. The wrongness.' Desh: 'I feel the ship shaking and four Force-users arguing about why.' Kael almost smiles. Almost.
emotional_trajectory: Residual tension -> quiet observation -> the smallest warmth

stakes.personal: Kael's first experience of being treated as a person rather than a category
stakes.interpersonal: Kael/Desh friendship beginning — the outsider and the practical man
stakes.external: Low — this is character breathing room

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — engineering crawlspace, Desh's domain
sensory_details: The ship's mechanical complaints; Desh's competent hands on familiar systems; Kael folded into an uncomfortable space designed for one person; the hydrospanner warm from Kael's grip
notes: Small but critical character scene. Ben observes from outside — close-third limited to watching the interaction, reading Kael's surprise at being treated normally. Allston-channel humor through Desh.
